text:
Alex: Heads-up — dedicated canary servicing reserved-capacity is showing a perf regression after today's runtime merge (PR #4521). p99 longseq latency ~2.8x, error rate stable. Investigating.

Maya: Thanks. Is this reproducible in staging? Any tracing / flame graphs yet? :eyes: 

Alex: Repro on staging. Running quick perf run:
```
./bench --model=gpt-long --seq=4096 --qps=50 --batching=auto
p50: 38ms -> 40ms
p95: 210ms -> 540ms
p99: 420ms -> 1180ms
```

Chris: That's huge. Which kernel got selected? Could be the new threshold logic in kernel-selector.

Alex: Kernel picker log shows:
```
selected_kernel: merge_batch_kv_v2
reason: heuristic_score 0.72 > threshold 0.7
seq_len_bucket: 4096
prev_kernel: merge_batch_v1
```

Maya: PR #4521 adjusted the kernel threshold table (changed 0.7 boundary). Running bisect now.

perf-bot: CI perf alert: dedicated-canary/longseq p99 regression +115% after merge 3f6a8b (PR #4521). Link: https://ci.internal/perf/2170000000

Chris: Bisect narrowed to commit 3f6a8b -> kernel selector change. When forcing kernel=merge_batch_v1 latency returns to baseline.

Jordan: KV cache metrics show prefetches up, evictions up 4x during the canary -> extra memory churn. Could be merge_batch_kv_v2 interacting poorly with prefetch window.

Alex: Quick local test forcing old kernel:
```
KERNEL_OVERRIDE=merge_batch_v1 ./bench ...
p99: 430ms
```
So kernel choice is the main delta.

Maya: Suggested mitigation: temporary override rule for dedicated canary to prefer v1 for seq>=2048 until we fix threshold math.

Chris: Also a small perf patch idea: adjust scoring penalty for KV-prefetch cost. I'll draft.

Alex: We're holding rollout for Dedicated. Not safe to continue - this hits SLA p99 targets for some customers. Reverted PR drafted: #4527 (revert 3f6a8b).

Jordan: Oncall will monitor canary after revert. Assigning @Jordan.

Jordan: On it. I'll post updated perf numbers in ~15m once revert is rolled to canary.

perf-bot: revert PR #4527 created by maya — running CI perf job.

Maya: Thanks everyone. Filed follow-ups: KERNEL-234 (test coverage for threshold table), KERNEL-235 (kv-prefetch interaction tests).

Alex: Summary: merge changed kernel threshold causing merge_batch_kv_v2 to be selected for longseq, which increases KV prefetch cost and p99. Action: hold, revert, follow-up tickets. :thumbsup:

Chris: :thumbsup:

Jordan: revert rolled to canary — p99 trending back to baseline. Will confirm in 10m. :white_check_mark:
